one_line: Recent AI developments include a compact reasoning model that runs locally, an AI-assisted proof of the Riemann hypothesis, physics-constrained chaotic system modeling, Apple's early work on a desktop automation agent, and a high-performance open-source speech recognition model.

stories.title: Thinking Machines Releases Inkling 2 Mini
stories.summary: Thinking Machines has released Inkling 2 Mini, a 26.4B parameter Mixture-of-Experts model that uses a looped transformer architecture to enhance reasoning. With a 20GB memory footprint, it runs locally on consumer hardware and leads open-weights models under 100B parameters on multiple benchmarks.
stories.why_it_matters: You can deploy a high-performance reasoning model locally on standard consumer hardware for inference and customization.
stories.editor_reason: Release of Inkling 2 Mini bringing high performance to local setups.

facts.claim: Thinking Machines released Inkling 2 Mini, a fast, small-footprint Mixture-of-Experts AI model with 26.4B total parameters.
facts.quote: Today we are releasing Inkling 2 Mini, a fast, powerful model that’s small enough to run on your laptop.

facts.claim: Inkling 2 Mini uses a looped transformer architecture that runs middle layers multiple times per token to enhance reasoning quality.
facts.quote: Inkling 2 Mini is a looped transformer, running the middle layers of the model three times for every token.

facts.claim: The model has a total memory footprint of approximately 20GB, allowing it to run locally on consumer hardware like laptops.
facts.quote: The total memory footprint of Inkling 2 Mini is ~20GB, allowing it to run on local devices such as consumer laptops

facts.claim: Inkling 2 Mini leads open-weights models under 100B parameters on benchmarks such as DeepSWE v1.1 and Vals Index v2.2.
facts.quote: Inkling 2 Mini leads every open-weights model with less than 100B total parameters on benchmarks such as DeepSWE v1.1 (48.2%) and Vals Index v2.2 (46.5%).

facts.claim: The model is released with open weights and is immediately available on Tinker for inference and customization.
facts.quote: Inkling 2 Mini is released with open weights and is available on Tinker today for inference and customization.

stories.title: AI-Assisted and Human Proofs of the Riemann Hypothesis Announced
stories.summary: Anthropic employee and mathematician Levent Alpöge announced a solution to the 167-year-old Riemann hypothesis developed using the Claude AI model. Independent sources have confirmed that the solution compiles in the Lean proof-verification language.
stories.why_it_matters: AI models are now capable of assisting mathematicians in developing verifiable, complex proofs for historic mathematical problems.
stories.editor_reason: AI claims a solution to the historic Riemann hypothesis.

facts.claim: Anthropic employee and mathematician Levent Alpöge announced a solution to the 167-year-old Riemann hypothesis.
facts.quote: Levent Alpöge: The mathematician saw his employer, Anthropic, become the first publicly traded frontier AI lab. He also appears to have solved one of the most important problems in mathematics.

facts.claim: Alpöge developed the solution using the AI model Claude, describing the experience as a stream-of-consciousness jaunt.
facts.quote: Alpöge described a “stream-of-consciousness jaunt through the experience of finding all the pieces of the argument through incredible confusion with Claude”

facts.claim: Independent sources and mathematicians have successfully confirmed that Alpöge’s solution compiles in Lean, an open-source coding language for verifying proofs.
facts.quote: Several participants in the Zulip chat, including MIT mathematician Andrew Sutherland, say they have successfully confirmed that Alpöge’s solution can be compiled successfully.

facts.claim: Stanford postdoc Alessandro Masullo also released a human-written proof of the General Riemann hypothesis without the use of AI.
facts.quote: Stanford professor and the president of the American Mathematics Association, posted a proof of the General Riemann hypothesis written by Stanford postdoc Alessandro Masullo, noting that “it is all human, with no AI.

stories.title: New Approach Enables Physically Consistent AI Models of Chaotic Systems
stories.summary: MIT researchers have developed a new approach to introduce physics-based restrictions on machine learning models for chaotic systems. The method uses energy-based constraints and a projection layer to enforce energy dissipation as a hard constraint.
stories.why_it_matters: You can now train machine learning models on chaotic systems with guarantees that their predictions remain physically bounded and realistic.
stories.editor_reason: New physics-informed constraints make AI models reliable for chaotic systems.

facts.claim: MIT researchers developed a new approach to introduce physics-based restrictions on machine learning models for chaotic systems, ensuring they stay within realistic bounds.
facts.quote: researchers with MIT’s Laboratory for Information and Decision Systems (LIDS) have found a way to introduce physics-based restrictions on machine learning models that can ensure that such models never exceed realistic bounds

facts.claim: The research team includes MIT graduate student Sunbochen Tang and professors Navid Azizan and Themistoklis Sapsis.
facts.quote: a paper by MIT graduate student Sunbochen Tang and MIT professors Navid Azizan and Themistoklis Sapsis.

facts.claim: The new method uses energy-based constraints and a projection layer to enforce energy dissipation as a hard constraint, guaranteeing predictions remain bounded.
facts.quote: We then add a projection layer, a component that adjusts how the model predicts the system will evolve, to enforce energy dissipation as a hard constraint.

facts.claim: The findings were published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences (PNAS).
facts.quote: The new findings are published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences (PNAS)

stories.title: Apple Developing In-House AI Agent to Control macOS
stories.summary: Apple is developing an in-house AI agent designed to perform tasks such as browsing the web, using apps, and writing code on macOS. Revealed through a job posting, the early-stage project could see a release as early as the end of next year.
stories.why_it_matters: Native OS-level AI automation will soon provide standardized ways to execute complex, multi-app workflows directly on user devices.
stories.editor_reason: Apple is reportedly developing a native AI agent to control macOS.

facts.claim: Apple is developing its own AI agent designed to perform computer tasks on behalf of users.
facts.quote: Apple appears to be working on its own AI agent to conduct computer work on behalf of users

facts.claim: The development of the AI agent was revealed through a job posting for a senior engineering manager.
facts.quote: spotted a job listing the iPhone maker recently posted for a senior engineering manager to oversee the creation of an “AI agent that can use a computer.”

facts.claim: The proposed AI agent will be capable of browsing the web, using various apps, and writing code.
facts.quote: It browses the web, works across apps, runs commands, writes and debugs code

facts.claim: Apple is implementing new warnings in macOS to discourage users from giving third-party agents full computer access.
facts.quote: the version of its upcoming macOS 27.3 will deploy warnings discouraging users from granting full access to third-party agents.

facts.claim: Although Apple is eying a release as early as the end of next year, the in-house agent project is still in its early stages.
facts.quote: progress on its in-house agent “remains in the early stages.”

stories.title: Reson8 Open-Sources Rumble-2-Flash Speech Model
stories.summary: Reson8 has open-sourced Rumble-2-Flash, a 0.5B-parameter speech recognition model supporting over 40 languages under the Apache 2.0 license. The model transcribes an hour of audio in about half a second while matching the performance of much larger models.
stories.why_it_matters: You can integrate ultra-fast, multilingual speech recognition into applications with minimal computational overhead.
stories.editor_reason: Release of Rumble-2-Flash, an open 0.5B speech model supporting 40+ languages.

facts.claim: Reson8 open-sourced Rumble-2-Flash, a new 0.5B-parameter speech recognition model supporting over 40 languages under the Apache 2.0 license.
facts.quote: Today we're open sourcing Rumble-2-Flash under the Apache 2.0 license. It's a 0.5B-parameter speech recognition model for 40+ languages

facts.claim: The model achieves an extremely fast processing speed, capable of transcribing an hour of audio in about half a second.
facts.quote: an hour of audio in about half a second, with over 7,000 RTFx on full batches

facts.claim: On a 302-hour call-centre benchmark, Rumble-2-Flash performs comparably to NVIDIA's much larger 30B Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe model.
facts.quote: on par with NVIDIA's Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe (30B) on a 302-hour call-centre benchmark

facts.claim: On the Open ASR Leaderboard multilingual track, the model achieved a 6.96% average error rate, outperforming larger models like Meta's omniASR-LLM 7B.
facts.quote: averages a 6.96% error rate across Chinese, German, French, Italian, Spanish, Portuguese, Hindi, Dutch and English. That's better than Meta's omniASR-LLM 7B
